# missense_residue_v

Every possible missense single-nucleotide variant of the canonical UniProt isoform of each
protein with a structure model, mapped to the residue it changes: one row per (variant,
UniProt accession). It says WHERE in the protein a variant lands and which structure model
file holds that residue; it holds no association statistics, no allele frequencies and no
observed-variant information, so a row does not mean the variant has been seen in anyone. A
variant that falls on more than one protein has one row per protein, so `variant` alone is
not unique and a join on it can multiply rows. ABSENCE: a variant with no row is not a
missense change of the canonical UniProt isoform under the map's annotation (VEP 115 /
Ensembl 115). It means exactly that and nothing stronger: not that the variant is non-
coding, not that it is synonymous, and not that it is missense in no transcript. For a
variant's consequence read variant_annotation_v or gnomad_variant_annotation_v. ALWAYS
filter on chr, and on pos whenever a position or region is known: the table is partitioned
by chr and clustered by pos. `variant` is a join key and an output column, not a cheap
filter. The results-api serves the same rows from the file this table is loaded from.

## Scan pruning

Partitioned on `chr`: a literal `chr = <n>` predicate is what keeps a query under the sandbox's per-query scan cap, which BigQuery checks against its partition-pruned estimate before running anything. Clustered on `pos`: an equality on these cuts the bytes actually billed but does not lower that estimate, so it never substitutes for the partition predicate.

## Columns

| column | type | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `chr` | `INT64` | Chromosome number, X is 23. Partition column: always filter on it |
| `pos` | `INT64` | Genomic position (GRCh38) |
| `ref` | `STRING` | Reference allele |
| `alt` | `STRING` | Alternative allele |
| `variant` | `STRING` | Variant identifier as chr:pos:ref:alt. Same format as the variant column in the association views, so it joins directly |
| `accession` | `STRING` | UniProt accession of the protein whose canonical isoform the variant changes |
| `gene_id` | `STRING` | Ensembl gene ID without version: the accession's gene whose GENCODE v49 span contains pos; NULL when none or more than one does |
| `gene_name` | `STRING` | GENCODE v49 gene symbol of gene_id; NULL with it |
| `aa_pos` | `INT64` | Protein position of the changed residue (1-based, canonical UniProt isoform) |
| `aa_ref` | `STRING` | Reference amino acid, one-letter code |
| `aa_alt` | `STRING` | Alternative amino acid, one-letter code |
| `model_file_id` | `STRING` | Structure model file that holds aa_pos. A long protein is modelled as several overlapping files; this is the one that owns the residue |
| `file_position` | `INT64` | Position of the residue within model_file_id (1-based); equals aa_pos only when the file starts at the protein's first residue |
| `mu_snp` | `FLOAT64` | Per-variant mutation rate; NULL where the source has none |
| `release` | `STRING` | Protein structure release the rows were loaded from; the same on every row |

## Worked examples

Queries that run against missense_residue_v as written.

### Which residue a variant changes. Filter on chr and pos (partition and clustering key), then on the alleles. No row means only that the variant is not a missense change of the canonical UniProt isoform.

```sql
SELECT variant, gene_name, accession, aa_ref, aa_pos, aa_alt, model_file_id, file_position
FROM missense_residue_v
WHERE chr = 7 AND pos = 140753336 AND ref = 'A' AND alt = 'T'
```

### Residues changed by fine-mapped variants on one chromosome. Give both sides a literal chr so both prune partitions; a variant on two proteins returns two rows.

```sql
WITH cs AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT chr, pos, variant, trait_original, pip
  FROM credible_sets_v
  WHERE resource = 'finngen' AND data_type = 'GWAS' AND pip > 0.5 AND chr = 19
)
SELECT cs.trait_original, cs.variant, cs.pip, m.gene_name, m.accession,
       CONCAT(m.aa_ref, m.aa_pos, m.aa_alt) AS protein_change, m.model_file_id
FROM cs
JOIN missense_residue_v m
  ON m.chr = cs.chr AND m.pos = cs.pos AND m.variant = cs.variant
WHERE m.chr = 19
ORDER BY cs.pip DESC
```

### Possible missense variants per residue across a gene's span. Keep the chr and pos filters: gene_name alone prunes nothing.

```sql
SELECT accession, aa_pos, aa_ref, COUNT(*) AS n_possible_missense, SUM(mu_snp) AS mu
FROM missense_residue_v
WHERE chr = 7 AND pos BETWEEN 140719327 AND 140924929 AND gene_name = 'BRAF'
GROUP BY accession, aa_pos, aa_ref
ORDER BY aa_pos
```
